notes: Primary failure candidate is index 1: 'runtime service startup timeout: readiness deadline exceeded' (RuntimeService, pid 2600). This is the earliest error-level event and directly names the readiness failure that the symptom describes.

Index 0 (ThermalHAL 'thermal sensor read timeout', pid 700) is a warning that precedes the runtime startup timeout by 100ms. It is a plausible upstream contributor (thermal throttling delaying service init) but is only a W-level warning; no deterministic causal link is established, so it is listed as evidence rather than a primary candidate.
Indices 2-8 (RuntimeService 'required service unavailable') are repeated downstream reports of the same readiness failure from the runtime service itself.
Indices 9-18 (Binder 'binder transaction failed: runtime service not ready', pid 2400) represent propagation of the unready service to binder clients.
Indices 19-22 (ClientRuntime 'app-visible startup dependency unavailable', pid 2500) are the app-facing manifestation of the unavailable runtime dependency.
Index 23 (AndroidRuntime 'FATAL EXCEPTION: main; runtime service not ready', pid 2500) is the terminal crash of com.demo.unready at the reported failure timestamp 15:00:03.

Indices 24-25 (kmsg 'container runtime readiness probe expired' / 'runtime dependency probe returned no ready response') corroborate the readiness probe failure at the container/kernel level, consistent with the runtime service never becoming ready.

The chain is interpreted as propagation (candidate) rather than proven causality: runtime service readiness timeout -> repeated unavailability reports -> binder failures -> app-visible dependency failure -> fatal exception.
